It reads compiler-artifact.yml, evaluates the provenance job's condition for a pull request, a push and a dispatch of another branch, and a push and a dispatch of main, reads each job's permissions and the order of the steps, and runs the step that requires the build job's digests with bash, as a runner does. It reaches no GitHub service.

title: A supersession's fail date is the successor's release date plus its stage window, or earlier
when: With successors released on 2026-03-01: supersessions are recorded for an alpha, a beta and a ga component with no declaration change, for a beta component with a declaration change, for a beta component with a fail date shortened to 2026-05-01, and for a beta component with a fail date of 2026-06-02.
then: Expects the fail dates 2026-03-01 for alpha, 2026-06-01 for beta, 2026-09-01 for ga and 2026-09-01 for beta with a declaration change. Expects the shortened date to be kept. Expects the date one day after the window to be refused, naming the latest date allowed, 2026-06-01.

title: The platform requirements state each need of the components, with its kind and shape, also when two needs have one kind
when: With the declaration and the registry of the test data set, whose components state one need of each of the nine kinds: Write the platform requirements runs; then it runs again with a second secret, payments-api-key with the key token, added to the needs of the SSO JWT verifier; then it runs again with one need taken out of one component's statement.
then: Expects each stated need to be in the written requirements, with its kind, its name, its shape (the keys url and password of the secret orders-database, the port 443 of the egress destination payments) and the component that needs it. Expects the second run to state both secrets, orders-database and payments-api-key with the key token. After the last change, expects the requirement of the need taken out to be gone and each other requirement to be the same.
notes: The data set has one need of each kind, so the second secret is the case that catches a derivation that keeps one need per kind. That the requirements hold no need that the components do not state is ST-DLV-DS01, which ST-DLV-DS01-T02 proves; this test does not assert it.

title: A need that holds an environment value is refused, and the requirements hold no such value
when: With the declaration of the test data set: Write the platform requirements runs once as it is; then once for each of four changes to one component's need, in which the need holds the secret value s3cr3t-password for the key password of the secret orders-database, the host name db.prod.example.com, the address 10.0.0.5, or the namespace orders-prod.
then: Expects the first run to write requirements whose entries hold only a kind, a name, a shape and the component that needs it. Expects each changed run to be refused with a reason that names the component, the need and the field that holds the value, and to give no requirements.
notes: The four values are one of each sort that the invariant names; the check of the written file is a check of its fields, not a search for known values, so that a value of a new sort is also caught.

title: The CI file holds only the pinned call to the shared pipeline and to the STEGO checks
when: With the declaration and the registry of the test data set: Write the delivery pipeline runs for the hosted CI provider, then for Konflux; then both run again with a registry whose pins differ.
then: Expects the hosted CI file to hold one job that calls the shared pipeline by its location at the 40-character commit, and the STEGO checks by their pinned reference, with no step, script or job of its own. Expects the Konflux PipelineRun to reference the standard pipeline bundle and the STEGO checks bundle each by a sha256 digest, with no inline task or script. Expects each file from the second registry to differ from the first only in the lines that hold a pin.

title: The pins and the trusted signer of the CI file are the ones the registry's ci-pipeline component names
when: With the registry of the test data set: Write the delivery pipeline runs for each provider; then the ci-pipeline component is changed to name other pins and another trusted signer, and it runs again.
then: Expects each pinned reference and the trusted signer in each CI file to equal, byte for byte, what the ci-pipeline component names at that run. Expects each CI file to hold no pinned reference and no signer that the ci-pipeline component of that run does not name: after the change, no value of the first ci-pipeline component is left in either file.

title: A candidate from either provider passes only when each of the five STEGO checks passed
when: With a candidate built by the hosted CI provider and one built by Konflux, and fakes of the five checks: Check a delivery candidate runs for each candidate with each check passing; then once for each check, with that one check failing; then once with the result of the executable match missing.
then: Expects both candidates to pass, and Delivery candidate passed to be raised once for each, when all five checks pass. Expects each other run to refuse the candidate, for both providers, naming the check that failed or that did not run, and to raise no Delivery candidate passed.
notes: The checks are drift, vet, test, the reproducible build and the executable match. The missing result is the case that catches a check left out of a provider's list.

title: A candidate passes only when its executable is byte-identical to the one its build record names, from either provider
when: With the build record and the two images of the test data set: the executable match runs on each image; then on a copy of the hosted image and on a copy of the Konflux image, in each of which one byte of the executable is changed.
then: Expects both images to pass, the Konflux image included, since buildah built it from the generated Containerfile. Expects each changed copy to be refused with a reason that names the digest the record names and the digest found in the image.
notes: The changed copy of the Konflux image is the case that catches a match that runs for one provider only, or that trusts the Konflux build in place of the executable.

title: The generated Containerfile builds with the network off, on scratch, to the executable the reproducible build makes
when: With the service of the test data set after stego apply, and its modules prefetched into the build context in the layout that Konflux's prefetch writes: buildah builds the generated Containerfile with the network off; then again with one prefetched module changed so that it does not match go.sum; then again with no prefetched modules.
then: Expects the first build to succeed, its final stage to be FROM scratch, its builder image to be the archetype's Go SDK named by digest, and the sha256 of its executable to equal the executable digest in the build record of stego build for the same revision. Expects the second build to fail naming the module whose checksum differs, and the third to fail without a network fetch.
notes: Runs on the developer workstation with rootless buildah at a pinned version (ST-STD-LOCAL). A build that downloads a module must fail the test: the build runs in a network namespace with no route out.

title: The Kubernetes base holds only what the declaration derives, with probes and default resources, and no environment value
when: With the declaration of the test data set, which has an ingress, an egress destination and a secret: Write the Kubernetes base runs; then it runs again with another working folder, other environment variables and an environment file for another environment beside the project; then it runs with the egress destination payments taken out of the declaration.
then: Expects the second run to give the same bytes as the first, so that no resource takes a value from outside the declaration. Expects the third run to differ from the first only in what refers to payments, so that each resource follows an element of the declaration. Expects each container to have the liveness and readiness probes that health-check derives, at its path and port, and the default CPU, memory and ephemeral storage requests and limits. Expects no resource to set replicas, no PodDisruptionBudget, no metadata namespace, no image named by digest, no host name, no egress address or address range, and no Secret data or string data.
notes: Check each resource of the built output, not only the files that STEGO writes today, so that a new resource is also checked. The invariant forbids an image digest; it does not forbid an image name or tag, so the test does not refuse one.

title: The Kubernetes base builds with plain kustomize and no plugin
when: With the service of the test data set after stego apply: the pinned kustomize version builds the base with the network off and with no plugin or exec option; then it builds an overlay fixture that sets the namespace, the replicas and the image digest on the base.
then: Expects both builds to exit 0. Expects the kustomization file to list only files in the base folder, with no remote base, no path out of the folder, no generator or transformer that names a plugin, and no Helm chart.

title: The delivery object takes its cluster, namespace and overlay from the environment files, never from the declaration
when: With the declaration of the test data set: Write the delivery object runs; then it runs with a delivery stanza that also names a destination cluster, a namespace and an overlay path.
then: Expects an ApplicationSet whose template names the service orders, the project orders and the base path, whose files generator lists the platform's environment files, and whose destination cluster, namespace and overlay path are each a parameter of that generator, with no literal value. Expects the second run to be refused, naming the path of each of the three fields in the stanza, and to give no delivery object.

title: A fill manifest that does not name exactly one known slot and one declared collection is refused, naming the field
when: With the built-in registry as the active registry and a declaration with the collection org-users only: the fill manifest reader reads seven fill.yaml files. The first names rest-api.before_create and org-users. The second has no implements field. The third has implements as a list of rest-api.before_create and rest-api.before_delete. The fourth names rest-api.no_such_slot. The fifth names no-such-component.before_create. The sixth names rest-api.before_create and the collection org-groups. The seventh names rest-api.before_create and has no collection field.
then: Expects the reader to accept the first and to give its fill value. Expects it to refuse each of the other six with a fault that names the fill and the field: implements for the second to the fifth, with the value it names for the fourth and the fifth; collection with org-groups for the sixth; and collection for the seventh. Expects no fill value for a refused manifest.
notes: The fourth case catches a check that finds the component and not its slot; the fifth catches a check of the slot name alone, as runRegistryFills matches today. The registry and the declaration are values in memory.

title: Recorded evidence holds the fill digest and the contract digest of the passing run, and keeps them after a later change
when: With untested-fill: compute its fill digest with fill.Digest and the contract digest of rest-api's before_create.proto, record test evidence for it, then change one line of its policy.go and read its fill.yaml again. Then read a fill.yaml whose evidence has no fill digest, and one whose evidence has no contract digest.
then: Expects the evidence in fill.yaml to hold the two digests computed before the run, each as 64 lower-case hexadecimal digits, and to keep them unchanged after the change to policy.go. Expects the reader to refuse each fill.yaml with a missing digest, naming the missing field.
notes: Compute the expected digests before the run and change the fill after it: a test that computes them after the run passes with code that computes the digests when it reads the manifest. Needs the Go toolchain to run the fill's test.

title: A sign-off is good only with a signature over the digest of its evidence, and new evidence leaves the old sign-off signing nothing
when: With unsigned-fill and listed-ssh: sign off the fill's evidence with stego fill sign. Make a copy of unsigned-fill whose sign-off names the digest of its evidence but carries a signature that listed-ssh made over another digest, and verify that sign-off. Then, in the first fill, change one line of policy.go, record new evidence, and verify the first sign-off against the new evidence.
then: Expects the first sign-off to hold the digest of the evidence and a signature that ssh-keygen -Y verify accepts over that digest with the public key of listed-ssh. Expects the verification of the copy to fail with the reason that its signature does not cover its evidence, and the copy not to be qualified. Expects the verification of the first sign-off against the new evidence to fail with the reason that it signs other evidence, and the fill not to be qualified.
notes: VerifySignOff are not built. Use the real ssh-keygen; a fake signer cannot show that the signature covers the digest. The copy catches a check that compares the evidence digest field and does not verify the signature over it. Do not expect a refusal to store an old sign-off: the second sentence of the invariant lets an old sign-off stay after new evidence, where it signs nothing.

title: A fill with no test file gets no evidence, and STEGO names it
when: With no-tests-fill and untested-fill: record test evidence for both. Then add a file notes_test.txt to no-tests-fill and record test evidence again.
then: Expects fill.yaml of no-tests-fill to stay byte for byte as it was after each run, and the output of each run to name no-tests-fill with the reason that it has no test file. Expects untested-fill to get evidence in the first run.
notes: A test file is a Go file whose name ends in _test.go, as go test reads it. The second run catches a check that looks for the word test in any file name.

title: A fill whose built files import anything but out/slots, the standard library or a listed fill module gets no evidence, naming the import, and its test files may import any module of go.mod
when: With a declaration that lists the fill module github.com/google/uuid and a project go.mod that also holds github.com/stretchr/testify: record test evidence for nine copies of untested-fill, each with one change: policy.go imports fmt; policy.go imports github.com/google/uuid; policy.go imports a package under github.com/google/uuid; policy_test.go imports github.com/stretchr/testify/assert; policy.go uses a message of the before_delete contract from out/slots; policy.go imports github.com/google/uuidx; policy.go imports github.com/lib/pq; policy.go imports the generated package out/internal/storage of the service; a new file testutil.go, which is built into the service, imports github.com/stretchr/testify/assert.
then: Expects the first five copies to get evidence. Expects each of the last four to get no evidence, with fill.yaml byte for byte as it was, and the output to name the copy, the file and the import path.
notes: Resolve github.com/google/uuid, github.com/google/uuidx and github.com/lib/pq through replace directives to fixture modules, and give the uuid fixture a package under its root, because the real module has none. Then only the import check can refuse a copy. The uuidx case catches a check by string prefix. The policy_test.go case catches a check that reads test files too (decision on ST-EXT-Q01). The testutil.go case catches a check that skips each file whose name holds the word test. The before_delete case pins the decision on ST-EXT-Q02: out/slots is the contract package of each slot, and a check that reads the identifiers of another slot's contract fails it.

title: Recovery completes an interrupted apply, and plan and drift refuse until it does
when: With a project with applied output and a new plan: Apply stops at each journal point in turn.
then: Plan and drift refuse while the journal is pending. After recovery the output matches the record and no drift remains.

title: A record whose input manifest disagrees with it is refused
when: With a record with an input manifest: The manifest's declaration digest or registry reference differs from the record's.
then: STEGO refuses the record.

title: Apply refuses a plan whose registry content digest differs from the registry it reads
when: With a plan from a loaded registry: The registry content digest in the plan is replaced and apply runs.
then: Apply fails with a registry error and writes no output.

title: Apply refuses a plan that carries another compiler build
when: With a project applied by the current compiler: The compiler build in the plan is changed and apply runs.
then: Apply fails with a compiler error and leaves the record unchanged.

title: Apply refuses a plan when an input, the record or a generated file changed after planning
when: With a project with applied output and a fresh plan: One of service.yaml, go.mod, go.sum, the record, the config or a generated file changes, and apply runs.
then: Apply refuses the stale plan, and the changed file and the record keep their content.
notes: TestDetectDriftFillPresence in the same file covers the fills folder: whether the project holds a fill is an input of the record (ST-BLD-INV07), so apply refuses a plan made before the first fill, and drift names fills/ when the first fill comes or the last goes. An empty fills folder is not a fill.

title: A generator that emits one path twice stops planning
when: With a project whose generator returns the same output path twice: Planning runs.
then: Planning stops with a duplicate path error that names the path, and no plan is made.
notes: Two components cannot claim one path, because overlapping namespaces are refused before generators run. This test covers the remaining case, one generator that returns a path twice. The same check in reconciler.go also covers the slot and assembler files, because they join the list before the check runs.

title: A generator file outside its component namespace stops planning
when: With a component that declares an output namespace, and a generator that returns a file outside it: Planning runs.
then: Planning stops with a namespace error.
notes: TestReconcile_NoNamespaceComponentProducingFilesRejected covers the second clause, a component that generates files with no namespace, but has no ID of its own; the one test record names the first case.

title: A plan that writes, deletes or records a path outside the output folder is refused before a fill changes
when: With a project with a hand-written fill, and a plan that names ../fills/policy.go as a file to write, to delete or to record: Apply runs the plan.
then: Apply refuses the plan, the fill keeps its content, and the output folder is not created.
notes: TestApplyRejectsReservedOutputRoots shows the other half: an output folder set to fills, .stego, go.mod or service.yaml is refused.

title: A failed validation, generator or assembly leaves the output and the record unchanged
when: With a project with applied output and a record: A run fails in validation (a missing generator), in a generator (it returns an error) or in the assembler (a circular constructor dependency).
then: The run returns that error, and every file in the project keeps its content.
notes: No saved plan exists yet, so the test cannot show that a failed run saves no plan.

title: Plan and apply stop at a bound fill that is not qualified or does not fit its binding, and write nothing
when: With a project in a temporary folder that binds three fills: planning and then apply run, in process, once with all three qualified and fitting; once with one fill changed after its qualification; once with one fill never qualified; and once with one qualified fill bound to a slot whose interface it does not implement.
then: Expects planning and apply to go on in the first case. Expects planning and apply each to stop in each other case, to name the fill and the cause (changed, not qualified, or does not fit the named binding), and to leave every file in the project as it was, with no saved plan, no journal and no change to the record.
notes: The qualification is Extending's report of each bound fill (ST-EXT-QRY02); the test reads it as the planner does, with real files.

title: The architecture view is the same with or without hand-written notes, network or home folder
when: With a project in a temporary folder: the view is derived once; then once more with a README.md and a docs/architecture.md that describe other components, with no network, and with HOME set to an empty folder.
then: Expects the two views and the two model files to have the same bytes, and every element of the model to name a source in the declaration, the registry parts or the wiring of the run.
notes: A guessed element is ST-GEN-UC08-R05's refusal; this test shows that no outside input reaches the view.

title: Every run that writes code, apply and recover, writes the view and the model file, and the record holds their hashes
when: With an applied project in a temporary folder: the declaration gets an entity, and apply runs; then apply runs again with no change; then one byte of the view is changed and drift runs; then the view is restored, the declaration gets a second entity, apply stops after its journal is written, and recovery runs.
then: Expects the first apply to plan, write and record the view and the model file with the code, with their hashes in the record. Expects the second apply to change nothing. Expects drift to name the view. Expects the recovery to leave the view and the model file of the second entity's run, with their hashes in the new record, and drift then to report no change.
notes: Recover also writes generated code (ST-GEN-CMD02), so a run that writes the view only on apply fails the last case. It needs the hook that stops apply at a named journal point.

title: The generated module file requires the runtime library at the archetype's pin only, and a hand edit of it is drift
when: For each archetype of the registry: a project is applied, and the test reads its generated go.mod and go.sum; then go.mod gets in turn a pseudo-version of the runtime library, a replace directive for it, and a requirement of a second STEGO module, and drift runs after each.
then: Expects go.mod to require the runtime library at exactly the version that the archetype pins and go.sum to hold the pinned checksum, with no other module under STEGO's module path and no replace directive for one. Expects drift to name go.mod after each of the three edits.

title: A generated service reads no declaration, scans nothing and registers nothing by name, tag or init
when: For each archetype of the registry, with a declaration that uses two modes: a project is applied, and the test reads every generated Go file with go/ast and builds the service.
then: Expects no func init, no import of plugin, no read of service.yaml or of an embedded declaration, no read of the binary's own file or build information to choose code, and no reflection on struct tags to choose what runs. Expects main.go to construct and wire every part in one fixed order, the same in two applies. Expects the only name lookup that chooses what runs to be the mode registry that ST-GEN-INV26 asks for, over component sets that the generated code wires itself.
notes: Decided reading: ST-GEN-INV26 asks for named mode sets selected by a flag at startup. Each set is wired by generated code at generation time, so the mode registry does not bind the declaration at startup, and the test allows it and no other lookup by name.

title: Planning and apply stop at a pin that does not stand unless it is overridden by name, and an unread lifecycle is not a pass
when: With a project in a temporary folder and its lifecycle records: planning and apply run with each pin standing; with a component digest superseded and its fail date ahead; with it past its fail date; with the runtime version past its fail date; with a withdrawn digest that the record already pins and its fail date ahead; with that withdrawn digest past its fail date; with a new pin to a withdrawn digest whose fail date is ahead; with the digest past its fail date overridden by name; with two pins past their fail dates, both overridden by name; with the same two pins and only one overridden; and with lifecycle records that cannot be read.
then: Expects the runs with standing pins, with a supersession whose fail date is ahead, and with the withdrawn digest already pinned and its fail date ahead to go on, the last one naming the digest as withdrawn with its fail date. Expects each run with a pin past its date, withdrawn past its date, or new to a withdrawn digest to stop, to name the pin, and to write nothing. Expects the run with the override to go on and the record to name the overridden pin and its reason. Expects the run with both pins overridden to go on and the record to name each of the two pins with its reason. Expects the run with one pin overridden to stop, to name the pin that is not overridden, and to write nothing. Expects the run with unreadable records to stop, to say that the standing could not be checked, and to name no pin as current.
notes: Decision of the Product owner on ST-DIS-Q01 of 2026-11-04: a pin to a withdrawn digest that the record already holds is refused only after the withdrawal's fail date, and a new pin to it at once (ST-DIS-UC07-R02, R03). The case of the withdrawn digest already pinned with its date ahead catches a check that refuses every withdrawn pin at once; the new pin case catches one that waits for the date for every pin. The standing is Distributing's (ST-DIS-QRY03); the test writes real lifecycle files. The fixture writes each lifecycle date relative to the day the test runs, so the test needs no clock seam.

title: The emitted failure record never formats its cause
when: Reports a stage failure whose cause panics when formatted, and the bare cause, into a buffer.
then: Expects the cause kept for errors.Is and errors.As, a five-field record with the fixed event, severity and message, the right stage, and an RFC 3339 timestamp.
notes: The subtest of TestGeneratedHTTPLifecycle that carries this ID runs, in the generated project, TestFailureRecordDoesNotFormatCause with TestFailureOutputHasDeadline, TestFailureOutputDoesNotRetry and TestFailureTaskNamesAreData of internal/compiler/testdata/service_failure_test.go, which assert the stage-name set and the bounded write, so the outcome is theirs.

title: The emitted supervisor waits for a canceled task
when: Cancels a running task that holds its return, then releases it; also starts the supervisor with an already canceled context.
then: Expects no return before the release, a nil result after it, and no task started after cancellation.
notes: The subtests of TestGeneratedBackgroundLifecycle that carry this ID run, in the generated project, TestCancellationWaits with TestCanceledStart, TestTaskSignal, TestParentCancellationBeforeChildPropagation and TestCancellationKeepsOtherErrors of internal/compiler/testdata/task_lifecycle_test.go, which assert signal handling and shutdown classification, so the outcome is theirs.

title: The emitted supervisor contains every kind of task abort
when: Runs a broken task that panics with a string, with nil, with an error whose formatter panics, in a deferred call, or calls Goexit, beside a peer that holds its return; the generated project runs this once more under GODEBUG=panicnil=1.
then: Expects the peer canceled only after the broken task's defers ran, no return before the peer's release, a failure without private text, and the broken task listed once as failed and once as aborted.
notes: The subtests of TestGeneratedBackgroundLifecycle that carry this ID run, in the generated project, TestAbnormalTaskExitStopsAndJoinsPeers and TestTaskFailureNamesExcludeCauses of internal/compiler/testdata/task_lifecycle_test.go, and TestAbnormalTaskExitStopsAndJoinsPeers once more under GODEBUG=panicnil=1, so the outcome is theirs.

title: The assembler checks task indexes and keeps task dependencies
when: Assembles with task indexes -1, 1 and 0,0, and computes the consumed constructors for a worker that depends on a store.
then: Expects each bad index refused and the worker's dependency chain consumed.
notes: Constructor resources are asserted by TestResourceArgumentsUseTheSelectedDatabase and TestInvalidConstructorResourcesFailAssembly in internal/compiler/resources_test.go; the index and middleware rules by TestConstructorMetadataIndexesMustExist and TestPrimaryMiddlewareSelectionMustBeUnambiguous in internal/compiler/constructor_metadata_test.go.

title: Every component's input check finishes before any component renders
when: With two components where the second refuses the declaration: run apply.
then: The first component renders nothing, and the run stops with the second's refusal.
notes: Known gap: wiring checks still run after rendering today (compiler-preflight-gap.md), so this invariant is partly false until they move.

title: A constructor dependency names exactly one producer
when: With two components that derive the same value name and a third that depends on it: assemble.
then: Assembly refuses and names the consumer, the dependency and both producers sorted.

title: The build target meets every active component's minimum Go version
when: With a component whose minimum is above the project's Go target: run apply.
then: Generation stops before any generator runs and names the component and both versions.
notes: TestPinnedDependenciesGateGoTarget in internal/compiler/dependency_target_test.go covers the dependency-driven minimum.

title: The input manifest is bounded, canonical and digested one way
when: With a manifest that holds 1025 files, an absolute path, a path under the output folder, or a serialised size over 4 MiB: save it.
then: Each is refused and nothing is written; the digest of a fixed manifest matches its vector.
notes: TestInputManifestRejectsMalformedState in the same file covers the other malformed manifests. TestInputManifestFillPresence shows that a version 2 manifest digests whether the project holds fills, and refuses a manifest whose fill presence does not suit its version.

title: A generated symbol never shadows a predeclared or startup name
when: With an import path ending in error and a constructor whose derived name would be NewError: assemble.
then: The import gets a distinct alias used everywhere, and the constructor name is refused before output.
notes: TestGeneratedImportsPreserveLanguageAndStartupNames and TestConstructorCannotShadowPredeclaredNames in the same file cover every predeclared and startup name, and TestAssemble_FillAliasConsistency in assembler_test.go the shared binding record.

title: A record is upgraded on the next run and decoded strictly
when: With a record that lacks the compiler build, then with one written by a different compiler build, then with one carrying an unknown field: run apply.
then: The first is completed, the second is a record change, the third is refused.
notes: TestStateFormatRejectsUnsupportedVersionsBeforeWrites in internal/compiler/state_format_test.go covers unsupported versions.

title: The assembler wires each declared mode as a named set in one binary that a repeatable mode flag selects
when: With a declaration of two modes, api and worker: assembly runs, the test reads the generated files and builds the service, and the binary starts with no mode flag, with --mode api, and with --mode api --mode worker.
then: Expects main.go to register two named component sets, api and worker, with the runtime's mode registry, and to hold one entry point with a repeatable mode flag whose default is all. Expects one main package and one binary. Expects the runs to start both sets, the api set only, and both sets.

title: A run that emits a concern's code emits its check, and writes no record when a check fails
when: With four declarations, each with one concern only (tenant isolation, authorization, idempotency, ledger): apply runs for each; then apply runs for the tenant isolation declaration with a registry copy whose component breaks the isolation check.
then: Expects each of the four applies to write the check of its own concern as a generated file listed in the record. Expects the last apply to fail, to name the check that failed, and to leave the record and every file in the project as they were.
notes: One concern per declaration, so that a run that emits only some of the checks fails the test.

title: Conflicting HTTP routes of two components stop the run
when: ValidateHTTPRouteGroups reads route groups in which two components register the same pattern on the protected multiplexer, a public route conflicts with the protected fallback, and a pattern is not valid; then planning runs for two components that declare the same route.
then: It refuses each group and names the component, and it accepts groups whose protected and public routes do not conflict. The plan stops, names the route conflict, and writes no output, no module file and no record.
notes: The tests in internal/gen/http_routes_test.go cover registration failures and the protected mount.

title: Two applies at the same time give one writer and no mixed output
when: Two applies of the same plan start at the same time on one project; then a process that holds the lock dies.
then: Exactly one apply succeeds, the output shows no drift, and the lock is free after the holder dies.
notes: TestConcurrentApplyHasOneWriter and TestProjectLockIsReleasedWhenProcessDies each carry this ID in a subtest.

title: A binding to a slot no generator invokes is refused
when: With a registry component that declares a slot no registered generator consumes, and a declaration that binds a fill to that slot: validate it.
then: The check reports a slot fault that says no resolved generator consumes the slot.

title: A binding to a slot that no active component or bound mixin declares is refused
when: With a declaration that binds a policy fill to a slot no component declares: validate it.
then: The check reports a slot fault that names the unknown slot.

title: A setting of a component outside the active set, or one its schema refuses, stops checking and generation
when: With a component that declares one string setting: validate and plan declarations that set an unknown key, a value of the wrong type, a setting of a component that is not active, and a setting that is not a map.
then: Each check reports a fault, and each plan stops with a config fault before any generator runs.

title: An undeclared change to a base entity is refused, and a declared one that moves one phase is accepted
when: The check runs in process with the declaration and the record of ST-GEN-TD01 as base and these heads: User.email renamed to contact_email with no schema change; the same with the rename user-email-rename and its expand step; a new entity Team with no schema change; the same with an add change for Team; base steps in another order; a base schema change removed from head; and, from a base with no step, a head that gives user-email-rename its expand and its contract step.
then: Expects the heads with the declared rename and the declared add to be accepted, and each of the others to be refused with a fault that names ST-GEN-INV33 and the entity.
notes: Not automated yet: the check is not built. The test calls the check in process on two declarations as values and needs no git and no database. Planned file internal/compiler/base_compat_test.go. Owner decision of 2026-11-06 (Q1): a removed schema change is refused, because the declaration keeps every change. Decision on ST-GEN-Q03 (owner, 2026-11-07): every change after the first release is a declared step, add included; stego apply writes the add step, and the check refuses a missing one.

title: For each kind, v1 and v2 share one database and read each other's writes, and v2 and v3 do the same
when: From ST-GEN-TD04, each kind of v2's six schema changes is its own subtest with this ID in its name. The migration job of v2 runs; a v1 and a v2 replica each write a row that the change touches and read the other's row; v1 restarts. The backfills complete and the migration job of v3 runs; a v2 and a v3 replica each write a row and read the other's; v2 restarts; v1 starts. In one more subtest, on a copy of ST-GEN-TD04 with its own commits: w2 opens user-email-rename (A); w3 keeps A open and opens user-locale-require (B); w4 contracts A and keeps B open. The migration jobs of w2, w3 and w4 run in turn with the backfill of A complete before w4, and a w3 replica restarts after w4's migration.
then: Expects in each subtest every read to see the other release's write, v1 to restart and become ready after v2's migration, v2 to keep running during v3's migration and to restart and become ready after it, and the last start of v1 to fail with ErrMigrationLedger before it serves a request. Expects the w3 replica to restart and become ready after w4 contracts A, with B still open.
notes: Not automated yet: schema steps are not built. The test runs the stego binary and the service binaries built from the commits of ST-GEN-TD04, on PostgreSQL in an unprivileged rootless container with CPU and memory limits; it is not a stress test. Planned file cmd/stego/schema_evolution_test.go.

title: A new database and an upgraded one give the same catalog
when: From ST-GEN-TD04: the migration jobs of v1, v2 and v3 run in turn on the database, with the backfill between v2 and v3; the migration job of v3 runs on a new empty database in the same container.
then: Expects the two catalogs (tables, columns and types, constraints, indexes and triggers, read from pg_catalog in a fixed order) to be equal, with no trigger and no email column left.
notes: Not automated yet: schema steps are not built. The test runs the stego binary and the service binaries built from the commits of ST-GEN-TD04, on PostgreSQL in an unprivileged rootless container with CPU and memory limits; it is not a stress test. Planned file cmd/stego/schema_evolution_test.go.

title: A schema step on a base that pins an old postgres-adapter is refused and names the release to deploy first
when: From ST-GEN-TD03 with a registry commit R0 whose postgres-adapter is 4.13.0: the base is applied at R0; the head moves the pin to R1, whose postgres-adapter is 4.14.0, and declares the rename note-title-rename at expand, and stego compat --base HEAD runs; then the base is applied at R1 and committed, and the same head is checked again.
then: Expects the first run to exit 1 and to name postgres-adapter 4.14.0 as the release to deploy first, and the second run to exit 0.
notes: Not automated yet: stego compat is not built. The test runs the stego binary built from the commit under test, in a temporary folder with no network. Planned file cmd/stego/compat_test.go.

title: A local part with the name of a common part is refused, and a new local part is added
when: With ST-SUP-TD02, the local registry also holds, one at a time, a part with the name of a common part: the component store-a, the archetype svc-arch, the mixin extra-mixin and the port store-port, each once as a byte-identical copy and once changed. Then the local registry holds only local-a. Each time, the active registry is composed from the two sources.
then: Expects each of the eight compositions with a same-named part to be refused, and the refusal to name the part, its kind and both registries, with no active registry returned. Expects the composition with only local-a to give an active registry that holds every common part at its common digest, and local-a.
notes: A byte-identical copy is a replacement too, so a check that compares content in place of names fails the test. Each kind of part is a separate case, so a check that reads only components fails the test. The two sources are plain folders named as the common and the local registry; the system tests of ST-SUP-UC02-R01 compose the same refusals from pinned Git sources.

title: Every file a component plans is in its own namespace
when: With ST-SUP-TD01, plan the example declaration of svc-arch and read the planned files of each component. Then add the fixture component bad-writer, with the namespace internal/bad, whose generator plans internal/store/extra.go (in the namespace of store-a), internal/store-extra/x.go and ../outside.go, and plan again.
then: Expects each planned file of the first plan to be in the namespace of the component that planned it. Expects the second plan to be refused before any file is written, and the refusal to name bad-writer and each of the three files: internal/store/extra.go with the namespace of store-a, and the other two as outside internal/bad.
notes: internal/store-extra is not inside internal/store, so a check by string prefix fails the test.

title: A component below ga that provides the port of a ga component is refused
when: With ST-SUP-TD01, add the component beta-store (beta, a sunset date 30 days after today) that provides store-port, which the ga component store-a provides. Then add it at alpha. Then add it with the port beta-store-port, which no ga component provides. Then compose a registry in which a ga component and a beta component provide one port, once with each source first.
then: Expects the beta and the alpha component to be refused, and each refusal to name beta-store, its stage, store-port and store-a. Expects beta-store with beta-store-port to be accepted. Expects both compositions to be refused, naming the port and both components.
notes: Each case loads the registry, as stego registry compose does; the add of beta-store is a load of the registry that holds it. The compositions are two plain folders, one as the common and one as the local registry.

title: A mixin that replaces a part of its archetype is refused, and a mixin that only adds is accepted
when: With ST-SUP-TD01, extend svc-arch with four fixture mixins, one at a time, each of which replaces one part: one lists store-a at another version, one binds store-port to a component of its own, one declares the slot before_create of api-a again, and one changes a convention of svc-arch. Then extend svc-arch with extra-mixin.
then: Expects each of the four mixins to be refused, and each refusal to name the mixin, the part it replaces and svc-arch. Expects extra-mixin to be accepted, and the active component set of the example declaration with extra-mixin to be the set without it plus only the component and the slot that extra-mixin adds.

title: A provider that puts another meaning in a field of a port fails the port's conformance suite
when: With ST-SUP-TD01, add store-b, a second provider of store-port that fills the field version with a count that starts at 0 where the port means a count that starts at 1, and run the conformance suite of store-port against store-a and store-b. Then record the other pieces of the bar for store-b and try to graduate it to ga.
then: Expects store-a to pass the suite, and store-b to fail it, naming the field version. Expects the graduation of store-b to be refused, naming store-port and its suite.
notes: The suite is the mechanism by which providers are held to one meaning (see the notes of ST-SUP-UC09). The fixture provider differs only in the one field, so a suite that checks only the shape of the field fails the test. That a default provider must be ga is ST-SUP-UC09-R02, not this invariant.

title: A slot that no generator of its component invokes is refused
when: With ST-SUP-TD01, add api-a with a second slot after_create that its generator never calls but names in a comment; then with after_create called only by the generator of another component; then with after_create called by its own generator.
then: Expects the first two loads to be refused, each naming after_create and api-a, and the third to be accepted, with the emitted code of api-a calling the service of after_create.
notes: A slot named only in a comment or a string of the generator is not a call, so a check by text search fails the test.

title: A ga component without each piece of the quality bar at its current digest is shown below the bar and still loads, and its new version is not released as ga
when: With ST-SUP-TD01, read the quality standing of store-a after each change, one at a time: its security review removed, its benchmark removed, its design review removed, its reference comparison removed, one generator file changed so that its digest moves and all its evidence stays at the old digest, and one output contract changed so that the digest of its contract set moves. With the security review removed, also run stego registry quality and stego plan of the example declaration of svc-arch. Then release store-a at version 1.1.0 at ga with only the evidence of 1.0.0, and then with the four pieces recorded at the digest of 1.1.0.
then: Expects the standing of store-a after each removal to be below the bar, naming the removed piece. After the generator change, expects it to name the security review, the benchmark and the design review as made at the old digest, and not the reference comparison, because the digest of the contract set did not move. After the contract change, expects it to name the reference comparison as made at the old digest of the contract set. With the security review removed, expects stego registry quality to exit non-zero naming store-a, and stego plan to exit 0 with store-a still at stage ga. Expects the first release to be refused, naming 1.1.0 and each missing piece, and the second release to be accepted at ga.
notes: Decision on ST-SUP-Q04, reading b: a ga component below the bar is reported, not refused at load, because refusing at load breaks every service that pins it for a standing that moves. The plan case catches a load that refuses it. The reference comparison is held to the digest of the contract set, not to the component digest, so a check that holds all four pieces to the component digest fails the generator case.

title: An archetype pins one Go SDK by version and contents digest, and a build with another SDK is refused
when: With ST-SUP-TD01, load svc-arch with its Go SDK pin taken out, with a version and no digest, with a digest and no version, and with two pins. Then, with the pin as it is, build the example service once with the pinned SDK and once with an SDK of the same version whose contents digest is different.
then: Expects each of the four loads to be refused, naming svc-arch and the missing or extra part of the pin. Expects the build with the pinned SDK to pass, and the build with the other SDK to be refused before it compiles, naming both digests.
notes: The build needs the real Go SDK: the suite puts the pinned SDK in a local cache keyed by digest and runs the build on the developer workstation (ST-STD-LOCAL). ST-BLD-INV05-T proves the compiler's own pin; this test proves the pin of the archetype.

title: A component that leaves out its layer, its part in a request flow or the side of a port is refused
when: With ST-SUP-TD01, load api-a four times: without its layer, without its part in a request flow, without the side of store-port, and with the layer middleware, which is not one of edge, authentication, handler, slot, repository, store or outbound. Then load the full api-a, build the architecture view of the example service of svc-arch, change one generator file of api-a and build the view again.
then: Expects each of the four loads to be refused, naming api-a and the missing or wrong part. Expects the view to place api-a at its stated layer with store-port on its stated side, and the second view to be byte-identical to the first.
notes: The second view shows that the view reads the stated role, not the generator.

title: Every service of an archetype imports the one pinned runtime library and no other STEGO module
when: With ST-SUP-TD01, load svc-arch with no runtime library pin, with a pin without its module path, with a pin without its version, with a pin without its module checksum, and with two pins; then generate the example service and read its go.mod and go.sum. Then add a component whose emitted code imports the runtime library at another version, and one whose emitted code imports another STEGO module. Then change the pin of svc-arch and keep its version.
then: Expects each of the five loads to be refused, naming svc-arch and the missing or extra part of the pin. Expects go.mod to require the runtime library at the pinned version, go.sum to hold the pinned checksum, and no other module under STEGO's module path to be required. Expects both components to be refused, naming the import. Expects the changed pin to be refused, naming svc-arch and its version, which must change.

title: A slot contract must be a protobuf service, and emitted slot code never gives a fill a framework handle
when: With ST-SUP-TD01 and ST-SUP-TD05, declare the slot after_create of api-a with the v2-noservice contract, which holds only messages. Then generate the example service with a fill for each slot of each shipped component, and list the Go types that the emitted code passes to each fill. Then run stego registry add on a fixture component whose slot code passes a *sql.DB to the fill, and on one whose slot code passes an http.ServeMux.
then: Expects the slot with the v2-noservice contract to be refused, naming after_create and its contract file as holding no service. Expects no type passed to a shipped fill to give access to a database, an ORM, a router or the network, and each type to be context.Context or a type generated from the slot's protobuf service. Expects each add of a fixture component to exit non-zero, naming the component, the slot and the type it passes.
notes: The list of framework handles includes at least *sql.DB, *sql.Tx, pgx pools and connections, an ORM session, http.ServeMux and router types. The statement forbids any object through which the fill could step around the generated checks, so a check that knows only these names and accepts a wrapper type that holds one of them fails the test; the builder adds a fixture that wraps a *sql.DB in a struct.

title: A component that emits a file that is the same for two contrasting declarations is refused
when: With ST-SUP-TD01 and ST-SUP-TD04, add the fixture component static-gen, whose generator emits internal/static/util.go with fixed text and internal/static/mod.go, whose text changes only in the module path and the package name. Then add varying-gen, whose every file uses a setting.
then: Expects static-gen to be refused, and the refusal to name static-gen, both files and the runtime library as the place they belong. Expects varying-gen to be accepted.
notes: The second file shows that the module path and the package name are normalised before the bytes are compared.

title: A namespace that is not a Go import path, or a library namespace whose last element is not a usable package name, is refused before rendering and is never rewritten
when: With ST-SUP-TD01, load the registry once for each of these namespaces, each given by a component whose generator writes a marker file when it runs: a component namespace that is not a valid Go import path (internal/store cache, with a space, and internal//store, with an empty element); library namespaces that end in main, in the keyword type, in the blank name _, and in my-lib, which is a valid path element but not a valid package name. Then load a component with the namespace go-services/worker and a library with the namespace lib/worker, and plan the example declaration of svc-arch with them.
then: Expects each of the six loads to be refused, each refusal to name the component and the namespace as it was written, and no marker file to exist. Expects my-lib not to be accepted as my_lib or mylib. Expects go-services/worker and lib/worker to be accepted, and every planned file of each to be under exactly go-services/worker or lib/worker, with the Go package name worker and the import path that ends in the namespace as written.
notes: The never-rewritten clause needs a namespace that a normalising step could make valid (my-lib to my_lib, go-services to go_services); a check that repairs the namespace in place of refusing it, or that plans files under a changed path, fails the test. The marker file proves that the check runs before rendering. TestLibraryGeneratorsCheckGoPackageNames in internal/compiler/go_namespace_test.go proves only the library cases main, a keyword and a space, so it does not prove this record.

title: A slot contract change that fails a FILE rule is refused under the same slot name
when: With ST-SUP-TD05, release api-a with before_create at v2-compatible, then at v2-breaking under the same slot name, then with v2-breaking under the new slot name before_create_v2. Build the fill of v1 against each released contract.
then: Expects the release with v2-compatible to be accepted and the v1 fill to compile against it. Expects the release with v2-breaking to be refused, naming before_create and each FILE rule that fails, such as FIELD_SAME_NUMBER and RPC_NO_DELETE as the pinned Buf names them. Expects the release under before_create_v2 to be accepted.

title: A ga archetype without tenancy or audit-log is refused, and an opt-out needs a reason, which is recorded with the service and not in the registry
when: With ST-SUP-TD01, curate svc-arch at ga without tenancy, then without audit-log, then without both; then curate it at beta without both. Then check example declarations of svc-arch that opt out of audit-log with the reason "audit is kept by the caller", with an empty reason, and with no reason. Then run stego apply on the declaration with the reason, and compare the registry folder with its commit.
then: Expects the three ga archetypes to be refused, each naming every missing component, and the beta archetype to be accepted. Expects the opt-out with the reason to pass checking, and the other two opt-outs to be refused, each naming audit-log. Expects the generation record of the service to name audit-log and the reason, and git status of the registry folder to show no change.
notes: Decision on ST-SUP-Q03, reading a: the reason is kept with the service, because ST-SUP-A1-SR01 forbids a run to write to the registry. A run that writes a list of opt-outs into the registry fails the last check.

title: A declaration that binds a mixin without a mixin it requires is refused, naming both
when: With ST-SUP-TD01 and the mixins durable-events and kafka-events, where kafka-events requires durable-events, check declarations of svc-arch that bind kafka-events alone, both mixins, and durable-events alone. Then add the mixins chain-a, chain-b, which requires chain-a, and chain-c, which requires chain-b, and check a declaration that binds chain-c and chain-b only.
then: Expects the declaration with kafka-events alone to be refused, naming kafka-events and durable-events, and the other two to pass checking. Expects the chain declaration to be refused, naming chain-b and chain-a.

title: event-publisher resolves to durable-events and kafka-events, with a sunset one ga window after its deprecation
when: Load the shipped common registry and read the mixin event-publisher, the registry's ga window and the date of the release that deprecated event-publisher. Plan a declaration that binds event-publisher, and plan one that binds durable-events and kafka-events.
then: Expects the sunset of event-publisher to be the date of the deprecating release plus the ga window in months. Expects the two plans to have the same active component set and the same files. Expects the first plan to give one notice that names durable-events, kafka-events and the sunset date, and the second plan to give no notice.
notes: The test reads the dates from the registry, not from a constant, so a change of the ga window moves the expected sunset.

title: A port whose conformance suite lacks a listed correctness test is refused, naming it, and the suite of authz-decision includes and runs the new-enemy test
when: With ST-SUP-TD01, give store-port the correctness tests round-trip and version-order, and load the registry with a suite of store-port that holds both; then with a suite that holds round-trip only; then with a suite that holds both under other names (roundtrip and version_order). Then list the correctness tests of the shipped port authz-decision and the tests of its conformance suite, and run the suite against a fake provider that answers a check with a stale relationship after a revoke.
then: Expects the first load to be accepted. Expects the second load to be refused, naming store-port and version-order, and the third to be refused, naming store-port, round-trip and version-order. Expects authz-decision to list new-enemy, its suite to hold the new-enemy test, and the run against the fake provider to fail that test.
notes: Decision on ST-SUP-Q05, reading a: a port lists its correctness tests by name (the field Correctness tests of ST-SUP-EN06). The third load catches a check that compares a count of tests, or a loose match of names.

title: The transactional-service archetype is rest-crud with its named parts, and a local registry cannot redefine it
when: Load the shipped common registry and read the archetype transactional-service. Then compose it with a local registry that holds an archetype named transactional-service.
then: Expects the parts of transactional-service to be exactly the components of rest-crud, the durable-events mixin, the controller component, the spicedb-authz and idempotency mixins and the ledger entity kind, with no other part. Expects the composition to be refused, naming transactional-service and both registries.

title: A controller on a provider without a fencing check runs one replica and never takes over an expired lease
when: With ST-SUP-TD01, add the provider component lease-store, which provides the lease port, first with no fencing check stated, then with the fencing check false, then true. For each accepted case, generate the controller of the example service and run it against a fake of the provider: ask for two replicas, let the lease of the first replica expire with no release, set the first replica as gone by an operator action, and then send a write with a fencing token lower than the lease holds.
then: Expects lease-store with no fencing check stated to be refused, naming lease-store and the fencing check. With the fencing check false, expects the generated controller never to have more than one replica active, whether the declaration that asks for two is refused or runs one; and expects no replica, the first or a new one, to take over the expired lease after the expiry, after the operator action, or after both. With the fencing check true, expects the write with the lower token to be refused by the provider.
notes: Each of a replica count, a lease expiry and an operator action is a separate case, because none of them alone is proof of ownership. The provider fake records each write and its token. The statement does not say whether a request for two replicas is refused or reduced to one, so the test accepts both and asserts only that one replica is active. What a controller on a provider with a fencing check does on an expired lease is ST-STD-TXN-R15, not this invariant.

title: A component version whose successors are not in the registry is refused, and each version that takes work from its factory must name them
when: With ST-SUP-TD01, add api-a at 2.0.0 with Hands work to store-a 1.0.0 and load the registry; then with store-a 2.0.0, which the registry does not hold; then with store-z 0.1.0, which it does not hold at all. Then, with fixture components command, query, worker and domain-probe at 0.1.0 added to the shipped common registry, load it with each of http-application 2.0.0, http-application 3.0.0, grpc-application 2.0.0 and grpc-processes 2.0.0 and no Hands work to; then http-application 2.0.0 naming command and query; then http-application 3.0.0 naming only command and query; then grpc-application 2.0.0 naming only command and query; then grpc-processes 2.0.0 naming only command and query; then grpc-application 2.0.0 and grpc-processes 2.0.0 naming all four; then each of the four versions naming all four while the registry holds no command component.
then: Expects the first load to succeed, http-application 2.0.0 naming command and query to load, grpc-application 2.0.0 and grpc-processes 2.0.0 naming all four to load, and each other load to be refused with a fault that names the component version and each missing component or missing name. The shipped registry, with http-application 1.14.0, grpc-application 1.16.0 and grpc-processes 1.4.0 and no fixture components, loads as before.
notes: Not automated yet: the registry loader does not read Hands work to yet. The test loads the registry in process from fixture folders. Planned file internal/registry/hands_work_test.go. Each case is its own subtest, with this ID in its name. External review of 2026-11-07: ship commands before the factory goes away.
